title: Claude Hopkins
summary: Hopkins was at the Apollo when Schiffman brought Hawkins to the Harlem Opera House.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What about the Claude Hopkins Band?

Oh, Claude Hopkins was, oh, you know, Claude Hopkins was at the Apollo Theater in 1934 when Schiffman brought me to the Harlem Opera House, he was right down the Street. So, at that time, we was (inaudible). We filled the house up. We kind of let Claude Hopkins feel (inaudible) for that day cause we had the people out there.
Then, I met Claude a couple of
times through the years, like he was at the Roseland Ballroom most of the time. Ovie Alston, I think, was the singer. Orlando Robeson was his singer also.

And then, I met him. Well, we played a lot of dances off and on. I went down to, when he took out J. Roseland (inaudible), I went down and played in his place. But, I mean, we saw each other like, say, like you and I are talking now.
I don't know where he is now, but I know he was up here at the Nebula for years. And, I think his theme right then, 'I'd Do Most Anything For You'. But, he was a sweetheart. We had a lot of fun.
